headline: Bahrain-Qeshm Sequence Is Documented; Kuwait Link Is Not
deck: Iranian and U.S. accounts placed the Bahrain drone attack before U.S. strikes on Qeshm; Kuwait reported hostile drones on Tuesday night without an established connection.
body: On Tuesday, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had used drones against a U.S.-operated radar at Sheikh Isa air base in Bahrain, describing the move as a response to what it called repeated violations of Iranian airspace by U.S. military drones. PBS likewise reported an Iranian drone attack on a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, the third in recent days after a roughly two-month lull. [E4][E6][E9]

Bahrain said its air defenses intercepted the incoming aerial attacks after issuing an alert, while U.S. Central Command said the drones aimed at a U.S. radar system had been intercepted without damage to equipment or personnel. Stars and Stripes reported the same Central Command account. [E3][E7][E8][E10]

Hours after Iran said it had launched the Bahrain drone attack, the United States carried out several attacks on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Al Jazeera reported. Ahmad Nafisi, the deputy governor of Hormozgan province, told Iran’s official IRNA news agency on Tuesday that the American attack had caused no damage to residential, commercial or infrastructure areas. [E1][E2]

On Tuesday night, Kuwait’s armed forces said air defenses were responding to hostile drone attacks and urged the public to follow safety instructions. Its statement did not identify a link to the Bahrain attack or the Qeshm strikes. [E5]

**The desk's reading.** The accounts establish a Bahrain-Qeshm sequence: the reported U.S. strikes followed Iran’s stated Bahrain drone attack by hours. They do not establish that Kuwait’s report was part of that exchange; it could describe a separate incident during the same period, because Kuwait’s account gave neither a shared target nor a connection to the earlier reports.

**The next test.** A dated official account from the United States, Iran, Bahrain or Kuwait that identifies the Kuwait drones’ origin or connects, or separates, them from the Bahrain attack and Qeshm strikes would distinguish a widening operation from a Bahrain-Qeshm exchange alongside a separate Kuwaiti incident.
